items.name: Longbow
items.intent: The ranger's baseline: reliable at six hexes, and one hex further if you are willing to pay double.

items.name: Shortbow
items.intent: Short in the draw and short in the range, but the only bow that will shoot for free.

items.name: Elfbow
items.intent: It does not hit harder than a longbow; it simply does not miss, and when it must, it misses twice at once.

items.name: Barbarian Bow
items.intent: A bow built by someone who wanted it to be an axe; it hits like one and aims like one too.

items.name: Javelin
items.intent: The only tier-1 weapon that is genuinely both — throw it at four hexes or keep it and stab.

items.name: Longsword
items.intent: The reference weapon: cheap-and-reliable or expensive-and-heavy, and nothing else to think about.

items.name: Halberd
items.intent: Two hands, two hexes of consequence: shove one enemy off you, or catch three of them at once.

items.name: Knight Shield
items.intent: A shield that answers back: brace behind it, or put its edge through someone's helmet.

items.name: Tower Shield
items.intent: It has no attack whatsoever, which is the point — it is a wall you happen to be carrying.

items.name: Fire Staff
items.intent: Burn one thing every turn, or burn seven hexes of ground once.

items.name: Frost Staff
items.intent: Frost cancels burn and amplifies the next physical hit, so this staff is a setup tool wearing a weapon's clothes.

items.name: Earth Staff
items.intent: The only staff whose power points the other way — it protects an ally instead of painting the ground.

items.name: Lightning Staff
items.intent: The longest reach and the hardest hit of any staff, and it will miss more than any of them.

items.name: Force Staff
items.intent: One attack and no power at all — but the blast scales on Magic as well as Precision, so the staff pays a mage back for every point of it.
items.source: settled content | 2026-09-02: Force Blast re-ruled to precision + half Magic at 1 stamina.

items.name: Holy Symbol
items.intent: A hand's worth of god: it hurts the walking dead and mends the walking living.

items.name: Priest Chain
items.intent: A censer on a length of chain — it swings at one enemy and blesses everyone behind it.

items.name: Pile of Rocks
items.intent: It is rocks. You throw them. They are free and they are accurate and they do almost nothing.

items.name: Slingshot
items.intent: A forked stick and a strip of hide, and it will still outrange a thrown rock.

items.name: Pitchfork
items.intent: Two hands and a farm tool's balance; it is a real damage point and a real apology.

items.name: Club
items.intent: A length of wood with the bark still on it, and it takes the strength out of whatever it lands on.

items.name: Dagger
items.intent: Fast, free and barely lethal — you stab with it mostly to keep your guard up.

items.name: Basic Armor
items.intent: One point of Health and not one word of drawback — the floor everything else is measured against.
items.source: settled content | 2026-08-27: slots 0 — tier-0 armor never costs an item slot (dedicated armor slot, one armor per unit). startClasses is the start-draw pool; USE is universal across classes.

items.name: Flowing Cloak
items.intent: It does not stop anything; it just makes you slightly harder to be sure about.
items.source: settled content | 2026-08-27: slots 0 — tier-0 armor never costs an item slot (dedicated armor slot, one armor per unit). startClasses is the start-draw pool; USE is universal across classes.

items.name: Nice Robes
items.intent: Good cloth, well cut, and the only protection it offers is that nobody wants to ruin it.
items.source: settled content | 2026-08-27: slots 0 — tier-0 armor never costs an item slot (dedicated armor slot, one armor per unit). startClasses is the start-draw pool; USE is universal across classes.

items.name: Ragged Hides
items.intent: Twice the Health of basic armour, and it takes a point of stamina every fight to wear.
items.source: settled content | 2026-08-27: slots 0 — tier-0 armor never costs an item slot (dedicated armor slot, one armor per unit). startClasses is the start-draw pool; USE is universal across classes.

items.name: Rusted Plate
items.intent: One point of Armor for four separate miseries — this is the item the armoursmith exists to replace.
items.source: settled content | 2026-08-27: slots 0 — tier-0 armor never costs an item slot (dedicated armor slot, one armor per unit). startClasses is the start-draw pool; USE is universal across classes.

items.name: Destroyed Mail
items.intent: Four Health is a lot at tier 0, and twenty Accuracy is what four Health costs when the mail is in pieces.
items.source: settled content | 2026-08-27: slots 0 — tier-0 armor never costs an item slot (dedicated armor slot, one armor per unit). startClasses is the start-draw pool; USE is universal across classes.

items.name: Barbarian Hide
items.intent: Light armour that buys stamina and luck instead of Health, with nothing given back.

items.name: Studded Leather
items.intent: Two Health, clean, no cost — the light band's honest baseline.

items.name: Heavy Leather
items.intent: The heaviest thing in the light band: it trades the band's own Dodge and stamina for Health.

items.name: Heavy Chain
items.intent: A point of Armor for a hex of Movement, and no other conversation.

items.name: Mismatched Armor
items.intent: Four pieces from four dead men; it covers you and it slows you and it matches nothing.

items.name: Creature Hide
items.intent: Something's skin, and whatever it was, things still seem reluctant to land a good hit on it.

items.name: Plated Armor
items.intent: The heavy band at full commitment: two Armor and four Health, and you will never dodge anything again.

items.name: Reflective Armor
items.intent: The only tier-1 armour that answers magic, and it costs three hexes of Movement to wear.

items.name: Soaked Plate
items.intent: Heavy plate with no penalty at all, which is the strangest thing in the band.

items.name: Martyr's Censer
items.intent: It burns something of yours to make the light. Every swing of it costs a little blood and buys a little more reach into the dark.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02: tier 3 had one priest weapon and two mage weapons, so a tier-3 reward mostly helped the classes whose weapons are unrestricted. Three priest and two mage rows close that, keeping each class's theme — the priest ranged and true, the mage ranged and magic.

items.name: Reliquary of the Nine Tears
items.intent: Nine saints wept into one jar. What comes out is not comfort — it is a very specific kind of attention.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02: tier 3 had one priest weapon and two mage weapons, so a tier-3 reward mostly helped the classes whose weapons are unrestricted. Three priest and two mage rows close that, keeping each class's theme — the priest ranged and true, the mage ranged and magic.

items.name: Chorus of the Drowned Choir
items.intent: Two hands, because the singing needs both, and the choir it answers has been underwater for a long time.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02: tier 3 had one priest weapon and two mage weapons, so a tier-3 reward mostly helped the classes whose weapons are unrestricted. Three priest and two mage rows close that, keeping each class's theme — the priest ranged and true, the mage ranged and magic.

items.name: Emberglass Focus
items.intent: A lens of cooled fire. One hand, because the other is usually busy holding something that keeps you alive.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02: tier 3 had one priest weapon and two mage weapons, so a tier-3 reward mostly helped the classes whose weapons are unrestricted. Three priest and two mage rows close that, keeping each class's theme — the priest ranged and true, the mage ranged and magic.

items.name: Staff of the Still Air
items.intent: Nothing moves near it that it has not agreed to. The air is still and so, shortly, is everything else.
items.source: Ruled 2026-09-02: tier 3 had one priest weapon and two mage weapons, so a tier-3 reward mostly helped the classes whose weapons are unrestricted. Three priest and two mage rows close that, keeping each class's theme — the priest ranged and true, the mage ranged and magic.

attacks.name: Shot
attacks.intent: The cheap, repeatable shot the whole class is built around.

attacks.name: Long Shot
attacks.intent: One more hex and one more point of damage, for twice the stamina.

attacks.name: Short Shot
attacks.intent: Closer in than a longbow wants to be, and steadier for it.

attacks.name: Quick Shot
attacks.intent: Costs nothing, so it is what you do on the turn you have nothing left.

attacks.name: Elf Shot
attacks.intent: Fifteen Accuracy instead of a damage point — reliability as the whole payload.
attacks.source: settled content | 2026-08-27 review: damage 0 -> -1, gains onHit: +1 Precision (stacking, for the Battle).

attacks.name: Double Shot
attacks.intent: Two weak arrows in the time of one good one; it is a spread, not an upgrade.

attacks.name: Power Shot

triggers.effect: push the target 1 hex directly away from you

attacks.intent: The hardest-hitting tier-1 shot, paid for in Accuracy and a hex of shove.

attacks.name: Crippling Shot
attacks.intent: Trades a damage point for two Weak — the shot you open a big enemy with.

attacks.name: Throw
attacks.intent: Ranged damage on a one-handed weapon, and the Accuracy is what it costs.

attacks.name: Stab
attacks.intent: Free, and better than a punch — the reason you keep hold of it.
attacks.source: settled content | 2026-08-27 review: crit 3 -> 6. | 2026-09-02, from the weapon outlier review: damage lowered by 1 — a 0-stamina attack does not also carry positive damage. Ruled.

attacks.name: Slash
attacks.intent: One stamina, one damage; the honest option.

attacks.name: Stab
attacks.intent: Twice the stamina for more damage, more Accuracy and more Crit — the committed swing.

attacks.name: Hack

triggers.effect: push the target 1 hex directly away from you

attacks.intent: Strong, cheap, and it makes room — the warrior's default halberd swing.

attacks.name: Cleave
attacks.targets: an adjacent hex and the two hexes adjacent to both you and it
attacks.description: An area attack across a three-hex arc. It does not roll to hit, so it cannot crit.
attacks.intent: Three hexes in one swing, at the price of never critting.

attacks.name: Shield Slam
attacks.intent: No damage bonus at all; you are paying two stamina and a cooldown for the Stun.
attacks.source: settled content | 2026-08-27 review: cooldown 10 — the first HERO attack with a cooldown; the engine has cooldowns on powers and enemy actions, an attack-cooldown field is a named gap.

attacks.name: Fire Blast
attacks.intent: The mage's repeatable magic attack, with a burn stack riding on it.

attacks.name: Frost Blast
attacks.intent: Same shape as Fire Blast, but the stack it leaves makes your melee hit harder.

attacks.name: Earth Blast

triggers.effect: push the target 1 hex directly away from you

attacks.intent: Shortest range of the staves, and the only one that moves the target.

attacks.name: Bolt
attacks.intent: Three damage at five hexes, bought with the largest Accuracy penalty at the tier.

attacks.name: Force Blast
attacks.description: Damage equals your Precision plus the party's Magic.
attacks.intent: Deliberately the only tier-1 weapon with one attack; the double scaling is what it bought.
attacks.source: settled content | RE-RULED 2026-09-02, verbatim: 'Change it to precision +1/2, magic, and stamina 1.' So: precision plus HALF the attacker's Magic, magic damage, one stamina — was precision+0 for two stamina, the worst damage-per-stamina in tier 1. Uses the same halfStatBonus field as the Ancient Tome's Read the Page (2026-08-27); the half rounds nearest, 0.5 up, per the standing rounding ruling, and the field is a named engine gap on both attacks.

attacks.name: Wrath
attacks.intent: True damage ignores mitigation entirely, and against undead it is two points better again.

attacks.name: Smite
attacks.intent: A point better than Wrath, with no slayer line and no Accuracy bonus.

attacks.name: Throw
attacks.intent: Zero stamina and +10 Accuracy against a damage point of negative one.

attacks.name: Shot
attacks.intent: Free, four hexes, flat — the cleanest tier-0 ranged attack there is.

attacks.name: Jab
attacks.intent: Tier-1 damage on a tier-0 weapon, paid for with both hands and some Accuracy.

attacks.name: Swing
attacks.intent: No damage bonus; the Weak stack is the whole weapon.

attacks.name: Stab
attacks.intent: It pays you a point of protection every time you swing, whether or not you connect.

powers.name: Block
powers.description: Gain Protection equal to 4 + your Armor, and lose 5 Dodge for the rest of the Battle.
powers.source: settled content | 2026-08-17 quality pass: '5 protection and +2 Armor for the Turn' was a flat number. Now it scales off Armor and each use permanently trades away Dodge. | 2026-08-20: "every use costs another 5 Dodge" was a per-use escalation. The stat loss is the rest of the Battle either way, so it stacks naturally without a counter. | 2026-08-20: the escalating cost is back. It needs no counter — a rest-of-Battle stat loss simply applies again each time, and there is no cap on it either. | 2026-08-27: description trimmed by ruling — the per-use escalation needed no restating: stat modifiers stack by applying again; the mechanic is unchanged.
powers.intent: The straightforward brace — a flat mitigation bump plus a pool of protection to spend.

powers.name: Cover
powers.description: Plant the shield: for the rest of the Battle you have +20 Dodge against ranged attacks and -10 Dodge against melee.
powers.source: settled content | 2026-08-17 quality pass: '+15 Dodge and 2 protection' was a flat number with no decision. Rebuilt as a directional trade that has to be read against the enemy list. | 2026-08-27: description trimmed by the same ruling.
powers.intent: Dodge for the fight you expect arrows in, and a liability the moment blades close.

powers.name: Stand Tall
powers.description: Stance: for the rest of the Battle you have +2 Armor and +1 Resist, and lose 3 Movement.
powers.source: settled content | 2026-08-17 quality pass: '+3 Armor and +2 Resist for 1 Turn' was a flat, decisionless number. Now permanent, and permanently costs most of your Movement. | 2026-08-20: "your Movement is 2 whatever it was" was a stat OVERRIDE — nothing else in the game replaces a stat rather than modifying it. -3 Movement instead.
powers.intent: The heaviest mitigation available at tier 1, sold at the price of ever being somewhere else.

powers.name: Flame Burst
powers.targets: a hex within 4 hexes and every hex adjacent to it
powers.description: Deal magic damage equal to your Magic to every unit in the blast, and those seven hexes become burning. It does not roll to hit, so it cannot crit, and allies caught in it burn too.
powers.source: settled content | 2026-08-19: power.fire-master.fireball owns "Fireball" — two powers with one name is the worst of the collisions. The staff grants the smaller baseline version. | 2026-08-20: ground layers are PERSISTENT and carry no number and no clock. A hex is burning or it is not. One layer per hex; applying a different one replaces it. See rule.ground-layers.
powers.intent: The blast is the smaller half; the burning ground it leaves is the real payload.

powers.name: Frost Nova
powers.targets: a hex within 4 hexes and every hex adjacent to it
powers.description: Deal magic damage equal to your Magic to every unit in the blast, and those seven hexes become frost. It does not roll to hit, so it cannot crit.
powers.source: settled content | 2026-08-20: ground layers are PERSISTENT and carry no number and no clock. A hex is burning or it is not. One layer per hex; applying a different one replaces it. See rule.ground-layers.
powers.intent: Seven hexes of frost is seven hexes where the warriors suddenly hit for more.

powers.name: Earth Shield
powers.description: The target ally gains 3 + Magic Protection.
powers.intent: Protection scaled off the party's Magic — a mage keeping the front line standing.

powers.name: Storm
powers.targets: a hex within 4 hexes and every hex adjacent to it
powers.description: Deal magic damage equal to your Magic + 1 to every unit in the blast. It does not roll to hit, so it cannot crit.
powers.intent: Pure damage where the other staves leave terrain — one more point, nothing lingering.

powers.name: Heal
powers.description: Heal the target for 1 + 2 x Spirit.
powers.intent: Doubled Spirit scaling is what makes a priest worth the slot.

powers.name: Benediction
powers.description: Heal every ally within 6 hexes for 2 + half your Spirit, rounded nearest, 0.5 up (aligned 2026-08-25 — the old 'rounded down' is superseded by the half-stat rounding ruling).
powers.source: settled content | 2026-08-20 sweep: "hero" in a mechanical sentence — the word everywhere else is "ally", and an ally shape already exists. Same effect, one vocabulary.
powers.intent: Party-wide healing at half the scaling — breadth instead of depth.

powers.name: Ignite
powers.targets: a hex within 4 hexes and every hex adjacent to it
powers.description: The target hex and every hex adjacent to it become burning. It does not roll to hit, so it cannot crit.
powers.source: settled content | 2026-08-20: ground layers are PERSISTENT and carry no number and no clock. A hex is burning or it is not. One layer per hex; applying a different one replaces it. See rule.ground-layers.
powers.intent: The terrain half of the fire enchant, on a long enough cooldown to be a decision.

powers.name: Block and Dodge
powers.description: Gain +10 Luck and +10 Dodge until the end of your next Activation.
powers.intent: The small shield's whole philosophy: not being hit is the block.
powers.source: 2026-08-27 workbook review — Deflect and Cut (the damage-dealing attack) is superseded by this power, ruled: "Block and Dodge is now a power."

powers.name: Light It
powers.description: Once per Battle, free: set a forest hex within 1 alight — the hex gains the burning ground layer.
powers.intent: The cheap answer to a forest, and the reason a torch is not just a lamp.
powers.source: Authored 2026-09-02: the Torch's option was written in its description only, so the merged R37 (trinket-is-a-stat-stick) correctly read the item as pure stats. The option was always the design — this expresses it in data, where the rule can see it.

enchants.source: settled content | 2026-08-20: onCrit is a real hook now, and this is the standard rider on a status enchantment — a crit deals 2 more of whatever status it already applies. enchant.bloodletting had it first and it is now the pattern. | Ruled 2026-09-02 (GEAR-DESIGN.md §3a): the enchant pass — every surviving ingredient is tier 3 and is found on a reward weapon or armor, never sold; the Forge sells the nine tier-2 buyables instead.
